/-- **Weil positivity fails when the von Mangoldt weights are tilted towards a real quadratic
character.**  Let `χ` be an even real primitive Dirichlet character of conductor `q > 1`.  For every
`t > 0` the weights `Λ(n)(1 - t + tχ(n))` give negative finite-atom Weil symbol energy on some
polar-constrained `C²` test.  At `t = 1/2` these are the von Mangoldt weights on the primes that
split in the real quadratic field of discriminant `q`, with half weight on the ramified primes.

On the tests `f_R ⋆ Φ_{χ, ≤4R}`, radical for both `ζ` and `L(s, χ)`, both zero sides are
`O(R e^{-R/2})` while `∫ |h|² ≥ c`, so the energy is `-t log q ∫ |h|² + o(1)`: the defect is the
logarithm of the conductor. -/

source_arguments.statement:
theorem suzukiWeilPositivePrimeSample_of_mem
    {t : ℝ} {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ suzukiXiSafeUpperHalfPlane) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : n ∈ suzukiArithmeticPrimeWindow t) :
    suzukiWeilPositivePrimeSample t z n =
      suzukiArithmeticScrewQuotient t z *
          suzukiWeilPrimeDirichletTerm z n -
        suzukiArithmeticPrimeTerm t n z

theorem suzukiWeilPositivePrimeSample_of_mem
    {t : ℝ} {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ suzukiXiSafeUpperHalfPlane) {n : ℕ}
    (hn : n ∈ suzukiArithmeticPrimeWindow t) :
    suzukiWeilPositivePrimeSample t z n =
      suzukiArithmeticScrewQuotient t z *
          suzukiWeilPrimeDirichletTerm z n -
        suzukiArithmeticPrimeTerm t n z
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hnData := (mem_suzukiArithmeticPrimeWindow_iff.mp hn)
  have hn0 : n ≠ 0 := Nat.ne_of_gt hnData.1
  have hnpos : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hnData.1
  have hlog0 : 0 ≤ Real.log n := Real.log_natCast_nonneg n
  have hlogt : Real.log n ≤ t :=
    (Real.log_le_iff_le_exp hnpos).2 hnData.2
  rw [suzukiWeilPositivePrimeSample, suzukiWeilTest_of_nonneg_of_le z
    hlog0 hlogt]
  have hexp :
      Complex.exp
          (-Complex.I * z * ((t - Real.log n : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
        Complex.exp (-Complex.I * z * (t : ℂ)) *
          Complex.exp (Complex.I * z * ((Real.log n : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    rw [← Complex.exp_add]
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring
  unfold suzukiArithmeticScrewQuotient suzukiWeilPrimeDirichletTerm
    suzukiArithmeticPrimeTerm suzukiWeilPrimeWeight
  rw [hexp]
  have hiz : Complex.I * z ≠ 0 :=
    mul_ne_zero Complex.I_ne_zero
      (ne_zero_of_mem_suzukiXiSafeUpperHalfPlane hz)
  field_simp [hiz]
  ring

prose.text:
Suppose hW is full positivity and Σ|qλ(n)|n^(-a)<∞ for some a<1. Choose
max(a,1/2)<b<x<y<1. The absolutely convergent quotient series is holomorphic
on Re s>a and agrees with the existing pole-removed Q=ζG on Re s>1, hence
on Re s>max(a,1/2). On Re s>b its absolute a-sum bounds its norm. The exact
quotient receiver therefore excludes ζ zeros on Re s>b. The primitive form
G=κ(s−1)e^P has no other zeros and κ≠0; Q(1)=κe^{P(1)}≠0. Thus Q is zero-free
throughout Re s>b.

Q is bounded away from zero on Re s≥x. To see this, suppose otherwise. Its
far-right limit is1, uniformly in height, so a sequence of small values has
real parts in a fixed compact interval [x,R]. Absolute Dirichlet convergence
makes all vertical translates a relatively compact family, uniformly on each
half-plane Re s≥b'>b (finite heads plus a uniform absolute tail). Pass to a
subsequence of translates and real parts. The limiting holomorphic function
has a zero inside Re s>b, but is not identically zero since its far-right limit
remains1. Every translate is zero-free there, contradicting Hurwitz's theorem.
This proves a positive lower bound without a zero-free hypothesis added to hW.

Apply the Hewitt–Williamson inverse theorem to the shifted absolutely convergent
series Q(x+s). The Dirichlet coefficients of 1/Q are absolutely summable at x.
Termwise differentiation of Q is absolutely admitted at y because log n is
absorbed by n^(y−x). Dirichlet convolution then makes Q'/Q an absolutely
convergent ordinary Dirichlet series at y. On Re s>1, the literal exponential
identity gives

    Q'(s)/Q(s) = Σ_{n≥2}(lam(n)−Λ(n))n^(-s).

Uniqueness of absolutely convergent Dirichlet series identifies every coefficient;
the zero coefficient is immaterial and the coefficient at1 is zero. Consequently
Σ|lam(n)−Λ(n)|n^(-y)<∞ on n≥2. Adjusting the two finite initial terms gives the
exact hypothesis of `WeilAbscissa.eq_vonMangoldt_of_weilPositiveFull_of_rpow_summable`.
Since y<1, that theorem proves lam(n)=Λ(n) for every n≥2.

Conversely, normalized lam=Λ gives μλ=μ and qλ=δ1 by the literal exponential
identity and Dirichlet coefficient uniqueness, so its absolute series converges
everywhere. Thus this absolute-quotient class contains no new positive producer.
The conjectured subpolynomial qλ square prefixes imply membership in this class
by the dyadic argument above, so proving that conjecture for every hW would prove
full arithmetic uniqueness. This explains why the easier-looking square law
still encounters the closed regularity wall.

## Cycle 5: reciprocal and quotient square mass (paper proof)

For arbitrary full positivity and every ε>0, both μλ and qλ=1*μλ satisfy
Σ_{1≤n≤N}|a(n)|²=Oε((N+1)^(1+ε)). This is a classical mean-value bridge
from the newly audited all-twist reciprocal bound; it does not establish a
bounded mean for the infinite series or any uniform quotient bound.

**Reciprocal.** Put δ=ε/4. The proved all-twist bound gives
|P_N(t)|≤C(N+1)^(1/2+δ)(2+|t|)^δ, where
P_N(t)=Σ_{1≤n≤N}μλ(n)exp(it log n). Set T=208(N+1).
The sharp finite Dirichlet-polynomial mean-value theorem gives
|∫_0^T|P_N(t)|²dt−T S_N|≤104 N S_N≤(T/2)S_N,
where S_N=Σ_{1≤n≤N}|μλ(n)|². On this finite interval, 2+|t|≤210(N+1),
so the integral is at most T C²210^(2δ)(N+1)^(1+4δ).
Divide by T/2. This proves the claim with 2C²210^(2δ), including N=0.
Only finite polynomials are integrated: no exchange of infinite-series limits,
no random twist and no exceptional physical orbit enter the argument.

**Quotient.** Put δ=ε/2 and use the reciprocal bound with δ. The classical
divisor estimate τ(n)≤Dδ n^δ and Cauchy–Schwarz give
|qλ(n)|²≤Dδ(N+1)^δ Σ_{d|n}|μλ(d)|² for 1≤n≤N.
Sum and use the exact convolution summatory identity:
Σ_{n≤N}Σ_{d|n}|μλ(d)|²=Σ_{m≤N}Σ_{d≤N/m}|μλ(d)|².
For m≤N, floor(N/m)+1≤2(N+1)/m. Thus the last sum is at most
Cδ 2^(1+δ)(N+1)^(1+δ) Σ_{m≥1}m^(-1-δ).
The last series converges because δ>0. Multiplying by the divisor bound
gives exponent 1+2δ=1+ε. N=0 has empty sum. Every premise is supplied by
full positivity or a proved unconditional finite-sum theorem.

/-!
# Finite valuation components of a supported Dirichlet exponential

When every nonzero input coefficient is divisible by p, convolution degree r
is supported on multiples of p^r. A valuation-k component therefore uses only
the first k+1 terms of the exponential. No infinite depth limit is exchanged.
-/

open Complex
open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilSingularArithmetic

theorem dirichletConvPow_eq_zero_of_not_pow_dvd {p : ℕ} {f : ℕ → ℂ}
    (hf : ∀ n, ¬p ∣ n → f n = 0) (r n : ℕ) (hn : ¬p ^ r ∣ n) :
    dirichletConvPow f r n = 0 := by
  induction r generalizing n with
  | zero => exact (hn (by simp)).elim
  | succ r ih =>
    rw [dirichletConvPow_succ, LSeries.convolution_def]
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro ab hab
    have he := (Nat.mem_divisorsAntidiagonal.mp hab).1
    by_cases ha : p ∣ ab.1
    · have hb : ¬p ^ r ∣ ab.2 := by
        intro hb
        apply hn
        rw [← he]
        obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := ha
        obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hb
        refine ⟨u * v, ?_⟩
        rw [hu, hv, pow_succ]
        ring
      rw [ih ab.2 hb, mul_zero]
    · rw [hf ab.1 ha, zero_mul]

theorem valuationPart_dirichletConvPow_eq_zero {p : ℕ} {f : ℕ → ℂ}
    (hf : ∀ n, ¬p ∣ n → f n = 0) {k r : ℕ} (hkr : k < r) :
    valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f r) = 0 := by
  funext n
  by_cases hv : p ^ k ∣ n ∧ ¬p ^ (k + 1) ∣ n
  · have hn : ¬p ^ r ∣ n := by
      intro hn
      exact hv.2 ((Nat.pow_dvd_pow p (by omega : k + 1 ≤ r)).trans hn)
    simp only [valuationPart, valuationMask, if_pos hv, Complex.ofReal_one,
      one_mul, Pi.zero_apply]
    exact dirichletConvPow_eq_zero_of_not_pow_dvd hf r n hn
  · simp [valuationPart, valuationMask, hv]

/-- Each component is a literal finite exponential polynomial. -/
theorem valuationPart_dirichletExp_finite {p : ℕ} {f : ℕ → ℂ}
    (h0 : f 0 = 0) (h1 : f 1 = 0) (hf : ∀ n, ¬p ∣ n → f n = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    valuationPart p k (dirichletExp f) =
      ∑ r ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
        ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f r) := by
  funext n
  change (valuationMask p k n : ℂ) * dirichletExp f n = _
  rw [dirichletExp_eq_tsum h0 h1, ← tsum_mul_left]
  have ht (r : ℕ) : (valuationMask p k n : ℂ) *
      (dirichletConvPow f r n / (r.factorial : ℂ)) =
      valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f r) n / (r.factorial : ℂ) := by
    unfold valuationPart
    ring
  simp_rw [ht]
  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := Finset.range (k + 1))]
  · simp only [Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => by ring
  · intro r hr
    have hkr : k < r := by simp only [Finset.mem_range, not_lt] at hr; omega

/-!
# Finite-type Weil systems: the continued Weil function

Let `a, f : ℕ → ℝ` be supported in `[1, N]`, and let `v` be a *regular* sequence: `v(0) = v(1) = 0`,
`Σ |v(n)| n^{−σ} < ∞` for `σ > 1`, and the Dirichlet series of `v` continues to a function `E`
holomorphic on `Re s > ½ − η₀` with polynomial growth on vertical strips (`RegularPart`).  Put

`lam = Λ ⋆ a + μ ⋆ f + v`,  `A(s) = Σ a(n) n^{−s}`,  `F(s) = Σ f(n) n^{−s}`.

On `Re s > 1`, `Σ lam(n) n^{−s} = −A ζ'/ζ + F/ζ + E` (`LSeries_finiteTypeSeq`).

**Master identity** (`master_identity`).  If `f(1) = 0` and `lam` is full-cone Weil-positive, the
continuation `Φ` of the Weil function satisfies, with `Z₁(s) = (s − 1)ζ(s)` and
`G(s) = ½ψ(s/2) − ½ log π + 1/s`, for every `Re s > ½`:

`Z₁ · ((s − 1)(Φ − G + E) − 1) = A · ((s − 1) Z₁' − Z₁) − (s − 1)² F`.

Both sides are holomorphic on the convex set `Re s > ½` and agree on `Re s > 1`.  Off `s = 1` this is
`ζ · (Φ − G − 1/(s − 1) + E) = A ζ' − F` (`zeta_mul_eq`).  At `s = 1` it gives `A(1) = 1`
(`dirPoly_one_eq_one`).
-/

/-! ## Dirichlet polynomials -/

/-- `A(s) = Σ_{1 ≤ n ≤ N} a(n) n^{−s}`. -/
def dirPoly (N : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℝ) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (a n : ℂ) * (n : ℂ) ^ (-s)

theorem differentiable_dirPoly (N : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Differentiable ℂ (dirPoly N a) := by
  intro s
  unfold dirPoly
  refine DifferentiableAt.fun_sum fun n hn => ?_
  have hn0 : (n : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by
    have := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hn).1
    exact_mod_cast (by omega : n ≠ 0)
  exact (differentiableAt_const _).mul (differentiableAt_id.neg.const_cpow (Or.inl hn0))

/-- `a` is supported in `[1, N]`. -/
def SupportedIn (N : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop := a 0 = 0 ∧ ∀ n, N < n → a n = 0

theorem LSeries_eq_dirPoly {N : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : SupportedIn N a) (s : ℂ) :

  · refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun n hn => ?_
    have hn0 : n ≠ 0 := by have := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hn).1; omega
    rw [LSeries.term_of_ne_zero hn0, cpow_neg, div_eq_mul_inv]
  · intro n hn
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hpos
    · simp [LSeries.term]
    · have hN : N < n := by
        by_contra h
        exact hn (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hpos, not_lt.mp h⟩)
      simp [LSeries.term, ha.2 n hN]

    LSeriesSummable (fun n => (a n : ℂ)) s := by
  refine summable_of_ne_finset_zero (s := Finset.Icc 1 N) fun n hn => ?_
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hpos
  · simp [LSeries.term]
  · have hN : N < n := by
      by_contra h
      exact hn (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hpos, not_lt.mp h⟩)

def finiteTypeSeq (a f v : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=

  one : v 1 = 0
  summable : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re → LSeriesSummable (fun n => (v n : ℂ)) s
  series : ∀ s : ℂ, 1 < s.re → E s = LSeries (fun n => (v n : ℂ)) s

/-- Ordinary coefficients of a formal power, defined by finite convolution. -/
def valuationPowerPolynomial (ell : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
  | 0, k => if k = 0 then 1 else 0
  | r + 1, k => ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
      ell j * valuationPowerPolynomial ell r (k - j)

/-- Coefficient of degree `k` in the formal exponential when `ell 0 = 0`. -/
def valuationExponentialPolynomial (ell : ℕ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ r ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), valuationPowerPolynomial ell r k / (r.factorial : ℝ)

theorem LSeries_valuationPart_convPow_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (f : ℕ → ℂ) (k : ℕ) (s : ℂ) :
    LSeries (valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f 0)) s =
      if k = 0 then 1 else 0 := by
  have he : valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f 0) =
      (if k = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0) • dirichletConvPow f 0 := by
    funext n
    by_cases hn : n = 1
    · subst n
      simp only [valuationPart, valuationMask_eq_factorization hp (by omega : (1 : ℕ) ≠ 0),
        dirichletConvPow, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      by_cases hk : k = 0 <;> simp [hk, eq_comm]
    · simp [valuationPart, dirichletConvPow, hn]
  rw [he, LSeries_smul, LSeries_dirichletConvPow_zero, mul_one]

/-- Finite convolution preserves every fixed valuation endpoint. -/
theorem tendsto_valuationPart_convPow {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) {f : ℕ → ℂ}
    {ell : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hf : ∀ σ : ℝ, 1 < σ → LSeriesSummable f (σ : ℂ))
    (hell : ∀ k : ℕ, Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => LSeries (valuationPart p k f) (σ : ℂ))
      (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (ell k : ℂ))) (r k : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => LSeries (valuationPart p k (dirichletConvPow f r)) (σ : ℂ))
      (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (valuationPowerPolynomial ell r k : ℂ)) := by
  induction r generalizing k with
  | zero =>
    by_cases hk : k = 0 <;>
      simp [LSeries_valuationPart_convPow_zero hp, valuationPowerPolynomial, hk]
  | succ r ih =>
    have ht := tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.range (k + 1)) fun j _ =>
      (hell j).mul (ih (k - j))
    have he : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
        (ell j : ℂ) * (valuationPowerPolynomial ell r (k - j) : ℂ)) =
        (valuationPowerPolynomial ell (r + 1) k : ℂ) := by
      simp only [valuationPowerPolynomial, Complex.ofReal_sum, Complex.ofReal_mul]
    rw [he] at ht
    apply ht.congr'
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with σ hσ
    exact (LSeries_valuationPart_convolution hp k (hf σ hσ)
      (lseriesSummable_dirichletConvPow (hf σ hσ) r).1).symm

/-- The full convolution exponential has a finite polynomial limit at each depth. -/
theorem tendsto_valuationPart_dirichletExp {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) {f : ℕ → ℂ}
    {ell : ℕ → ℝ} (h0 : f 0 = 0) (h1 : f 1 = 0)
    (hsupport : ∀ n, ¬p ∣ n → f n = 0)
    (hf : ∀ σ : ℝ, 1 < σ → LSeriesSummable f (σ : ℂ))
    (hell : ∀ k : ℕ, Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => LSeries (valuationPart p k f) (σ : ℂ))
      (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (ell k : ℂ))) (k : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun σ : ℝ => LSeries (valuationPart p k (dirichletExp f)) (σ : ℂ))
      (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (valuationExponentialPolynomial ell k : ℂ)) := by
  have ht := tendsto_finsetSum (Finset.range (k + 1)) fun r _ =>
    (tendsto_valuationPart_convPow hp hf hell r k).const_mul ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹)
  have he : (∑ r ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
      (r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ * (valuationPowerPolynomial ell r k : ℂ)) =
      (valuationExponentialPolynomial ell k : ℂ) := by
    simp only [valuationExponentialPolynomial, Complex.ofReal_sum]
    push_cast
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun r _ => by ring
  rw [he] at ht
  apply ht.congr'
  filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with σ hσ
  rw [valuationPart_dirichletExp_finite h0 h1 hsupport,
    LSeries_sum (fun r _ => (summable_valuationPart p k
      (lseriesSummable_dirichletConvPow (hf σ hσ) r).1).smul ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹))]
  simp only [LSeries_smul]

/-!
# The finite part of the literal source harmonic sum

Ordinary convergence of the centered source series at `5 / 8` gives a
quantitative tail at `1`. Adding the Euler constant correction identifies
one fixed real finite part, with error bounded by a constant times `N ^ (-3 / 8)`.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology
open GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilSpectral
open WeilWorkSettledPhase
variable {lam : ℕ → ℝ}

/-- The literal source harmonic sum, including its coefficient at one. -/
def quantizationHarmonicSum (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (sourceCoeff lam n).re / n

/-- The centered ordinary Dirichlet value plus the Euler constant correction. -/
def quantizationHarmonicFinitePart (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) : ℝ :=
  (dirichletSum (fun n => sourceCoeff lam (n + 1) - sourceCompletion hW 1) 1).re +
    (sourceCompletion hW 1).re * Real.eulerMascheroniConstant

private theorem sum_Icc_one_eq_range {A : Type*} [AddCommMonoid A]
    (f : ℕ → A) (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f n = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, f (n + 1) := by
  rw [← Finset.Ico_add_one_right_eq_Icc, Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sum_range]
  simp [Nat.add_comm]

theorem quantizationHarmonicSum_centered (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) (N : ℕ) :
    (dirichletPartialSum
      (fun n => sourceCoeff lam (n + 1) - sourceCompletion hW 1) N 1).re =
        quantizationHarmonicSum lam N - (sourceCompletion hW 1).re * (harmonic N : ℝ) := by
  rw [quantizationHarmonicSum, sum_Icc_one_eq_range]
  have hh : (harmonic N : ℝ) = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (1 : ℝ) / (n + 1) := by
    simp [harmonic, one_div]
  rw [hh, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  simp only [dirichletPartialSum, Complex.re_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro n hn
  simp only [Complex.cpow_neg_one, ← div_eq_mul_inv, Complex.div_ofReal_re,
    Complex.sub_re, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, sub_div, mul_one_div]

private theorem harmonic_euler_error (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    |(harmonic N : ℝ) - Real.log N - Real.eulerMascheroniConstant| ≤ 1 / (N : ℝ) := by
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast hN
  have hlo := Real.eulerMascheroniConstant_lt_eulerMascheroniSeq' N
  have hhi := Real.eulerMascheroniSeq_lt_eulerMascheroniConstant N
  simp only [Real.eulerMascheroniSeq', if_neg (by omega : N ≠ 0)] at hlo
  simp only [Real.eulerMascheroniSeq] at hhi
  rw [abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
  have hlog : Real.log ((N : ℝ) + 1) - Real.log N ≤ 1 / (N : ℝ) := by
    rw [← Real.log_div (by positivity) hpos.ne']
    calc
      _ ≤ ((N : ℝ) + 1) / N - 1 := Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos (by positivity)
      _ = 1 / (N : ℝ) := by field_simp; ring
  linarith

/-- The centered harmonic tail is controlled by ordinary source convergence. -/
theorem quantization_centered_harmonic_tail (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N →
      ‖dirichletSum (fun n => sourceCoeff lam (n + 1) - sourceCompletion hW 1) 1 -
        dirichletPartialSum
          (fun n => sourceCoeff lam (n + 1) - sourceCompletion hW 1) N 1‖ ≤
            C * (N : ℝ) ^ (-(3 / 8 : ℝ)) := by
  let a : ℕ → ℂ := fun n => sourceCoeff lam (n + 1) - sourceCompletion hW 1
  have hconv := centered_forward_dirichletConvergesAt hW (s := (5 / 8 : ℂ)) (by norm_num)
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le.mp hconv.choose_spec.cauchySeq.isBounded_range
  have hbound : ∀ N, ‖dirichletPartialSum a N (5 / 8)‖ ≤ C :=
    fun N => hC _ (Set.mem_range_self N)
  have hC0 : 0 ≤ C := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hbound 0)
  refine ⟨4 * C, by positivity, fun N hN => ?_⟩
  have ht := norm_dirichletSum_sub_partialSum_le hbound
    (s := 1) (by norm_num) (centered_forward_dirichletConvergesAt hW (by norm_num)) N
  have he : (1 : ℂ) - 5 / 8 = ((3 / 8 : ℝ) : ℂ) := by norm_num
  rw [he] at ht
  norm_num [Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs] at ht
  have ht' : ‖dirichletSum a 1 - dirichletPartialSum a N 1‖ ≤
      4 * C * ((N : ℝ) + 1) ^ (-(3 / 8 : ℝ)) := by
    convert ht using 1; ring
  have hp : (0 : ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast hN
  exact ht'.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos (y := (N : ℝ) + 1)
      (z := -(3 / 8 : ℝ)) hp (by linarith) (by norm_num)) (by positivity))

/-- The finite part and its power-saving error for every full-positive source. -/
theorem quantizationHarmonicFinitePart_error (hW : WeilPositiveFull lam) :

/-!

This file places the finite-aperture pole and prime-power channels of the critical-Mellin
Stieltjes distribution inside the source-native continuous dual on the physical horizon `[0,1]`.
The logarithmic coordinate `h in [0,2a]` is sent to `omega = 1 - h/(2a)`.  The pole channel is a
bounded interval-integral functional; the prime channel is the literal finite von-Mangoldt atomic
sum.  They remain separate before being added.

At every physical mode, horizon reflection negates the sine test.  Consequently the combined
continuous source value is exactly the published polar--prime CCM sine coefficient, including all
signs and the factor of `pi`.  This is unconditional.  It identifies one literal arithmetic
channel of the source quotient; it does not prove positivity of the completed CCM matrix.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

open Matrix MeasureTheory Set

/-- Continuous logarithmic-to-horizon map, clamped outside the physical aperture. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon (a : ℝ) : C(ℝ, CCMGuinandWeilHorizon) := by
  refine ⟨fun h => Set.projIcc 0 1 (by norm_num)
      (1 - h / (2 * a)), ?_⟩
  fun_prop

/-- On the physical logarithmic aperture, the clamped map is the literal affine coordinate. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon_coe_of_mem {a h : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hh : h ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (2 * a)) :
    (ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon a h).1 = 1 - h / (2 * a) := by
  have hx : 1 - h / (2 * a) ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 := by
    constructor
    · have hdiv : h / (2 * a) ≤ 1 := (div_le_one (by positivity)).2 hh.2
      linarith
    · have hdiv : 0 ≤ h / (2 * a) := div_nonneg hh.1 (by positivity)
      linarith
  change (Set.projIcc 0 1 (by norm_num) (1 - h / (2 * a)) : ℝ) = _
  rw [Set.coe_projIcc, min_eq_right hx.2, max_eq_right hx.1]

/-- Prime-power indices visible below logarithmic aperture `2a`. -/
abbrev CCMGuinandWeilPrimeIndex (a : ℝ) :=
  {k : ℕ // k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2 * a)⌋₊}

/-- Every visible prime-power logarithm lies in the closed logarithmic aperture. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilPrimeLog_mem {a : ℝ} {k : ℕ}
    (hk : k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 ⌊Real.exp (2 * a)⌋₊) :
    Real.log k ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (2 * a) := by
  have hk' := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hk
  have hkpos : (0 : ℝ) < (k : ℝ) := by
    exact_mod_cast (show 0 < k by omega)
  have hkle : (k : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp (2 * a) := by
    calc
      (k : ℝ) ≤ (⌊Real.exp (2 * a)⌋₊ : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hk'.2
      _ ≤ Real.exp (2 * a) := Nat.floor_le (Real.exp_pos _).le
  exact ⟨Real.log_nonneg (by exact_mod_cast (show 1 ≤ k by omega)),
    (Real.log_le_iff_le_exp hkpos).mpr hkle⟩

/-- Literal horizon location of a visible prime-power atom. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilPrimeHorizon {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (k : CCMGuinandWeilPrimeIndex a) : CCMGuinandWeilHorizon := by
  refine ⟨1 - Real.log k.1 / (2 * a), ?_⟩
  have hlog := ccmGuinandWeilPrimeLog_mem k.2
  constructor
  · have := (div_le_one (by positivity : 0 < 2 * a)).2 hlog.2
    linarith
  · have := div_nonneg hlog.1 (by positivity : 0 ≤ 2 * a)
    linarith

/-- The continuous logarithmic map agrees with the literal prime horizon. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon_log_eq_primeHorizon {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (k : CCMGuinandWeilPrimeIndex a) :
    ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon a (Real.log k.1) =
      ccmGuinandWeilPrimeHorizon ha k := by
  ext
  rw [ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon_coe_of_mem ha
    (ccmGuinandWeilPrimeLog_mem k.2)]

/-- At a physical mode, affine horizon transport negates the logarithmic sine test. -/
theorem ccmGuinandWeilSineCoordinate_logToHorizon {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (n : ℕ) {h : ℝ} (hh : h ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (2 * a)) :
    ccmGuinandWeilSineCoordinate (n : ℤ) (ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon a h) =
      -Real.sin (ccmPublishedPhysicalFrequency a n * h) := by
  rw [show ccmGuinandWeilSineCoordinate (n : ℤ) (ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon a h) =
      Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * (ccmGuinandWeilLogToHorizon a h).1 * (n : ℝ)) by rfl,

    rw [ccmPublishedPhysicalFrequency]

/-- Literal finite critical-weight prime-power source channel. -/
def ccmGuinandWeilPrimeSourceFunctional (a : ℝ) :

Integrating the endpoint distance, instead of a single cutoff, retains the
logarithmic Poisson smoothing rate. The final weight adapts to the height.
-/

/-- A continuous endpoint envelope, including the two jump locations. -/
theorem windowError_le_endpoint_envelope {η y r : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    windowError η y r ≤ 8 * η / (η + |y - r|) + 8 * η / (η + |y + r|) := by
  let d := min |y - r| |y + r|
  have hd : 0 ≤ d := le_min (abs_nonneg _) (abs_nonneg _)
  have hb : windowError η y r ≤ 8 * η / (η + d) := by
    by_cases h : d ≤ η
    · refine (windowError_le_pi hη hy r).trans ?_
      apply (le_div_iff₀ (by positivity : 0 < η + d)).mpr
      nlinarith [Real.pi_lt_four, Real.pi_pos]
    · have hpos : 0 < d := hη.trans (lt_of_not_ge h)
      refine (windowError_le_endpoint hη hpos hy (min_le_right _ _) (min_le_left _ _)).trans ?_
      apply (div_le_div_iff₀ hpos (by positivity : 0 < η + d)).mpr
      nlinarith
  refine hb.trans ?_
  dsimp [d]
  rcases le_total |y - r| |y + r| with h | h
  · rw [min_eq_left h]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_right (by positivity)
  · rw [min_eq_right h]
    exact le_add_of_nonneg_left (by positivity)

private theorem integral_inv_add_abs {η R : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) (hR : 0 ≤ R) :
    (∫ x in -R..R, (η + |x|)⁻¹) = 2 * Real.log (1 + R / η) := by
  have hc : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => (η + |x|)⁻¹) :=
    (continuous_const.add continuous_abs).inv₀ (fun _ => by dsimp; positivity)
  have hp : (∫ x in 0..R, (η + |x|)⁻¹) = Real.log (1 + R / η) := by
    calc
      (∫ x in 0..R, (η + |x|)⁻¹) = ∫ x in 0..R, (η + x)⁻¹ := by
        apply intervalIntegral.integral_congr
        intro x hx
        rw [uIcc_of_le hR] at hx
        simp only [abs_of_nonneg hx.1]
      _ = ∫ x in η..(η + R), x⁻¹ := by
        simpa only [add_zero] using intervalIntegral.integral_comp_add_left
          (fun x : ℝ => x⁻¹) η (a := 0) (b := R)
      _ = Real.log ((η + R) / η) := integral_inv_of_pos hη (by positivity)
      _ = _ := by congr 1; field_simp
  have hn : (∫ x in -R..0, (η + |x|)⁻¹) = ∫ x in 0..R, (η + |x|)⁻¹ := by
    simpa using (intervalIntegral.integral_comp_neg (fun x : ℝ => (η + |x|)⁻¹)
      (a := 0) (b := R)).symm
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals
    (hc.intervalIntegrable (-R) 0) (hc.intervalIntegrable 0 R), hn, hp]
  ring

private theorem integral_endpoint_envelope_le {η Y r : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η)
    (hY : 1 ≤ Y) (hr : |r| ≤ 4 * Y) :
    (∫ y in Ioc Y (2 * Y), (η + |y - r|)⁻¹) ≤
      2 * Real.log (1 + 6 * Y / η) := by
  have hc : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => (η + |x|)⁻¹) :=
    (continuous_const.add continuous_abs).inv₀ (fun _ => by dsimp; positivity)
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (by linarith : Y ≤ 2 * Y),
    intervalIntegral.integral_comp_sub_right (fun x : ℝ => (η + |x|)⁻¹) r]
  refine (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval (c := -(6 * Y)) (d := 6 * Y)
    (by linarith [(abs_le.mp hr).2]) (by linarith)
    (by linarith [(abs_le.mp hr).1]) (Eventually.of_forall fun x => by positivity)
    (hc.intervalIntegrable _ _)).trans_eq ?_
  exact integral_inv_add_abs hη (by linarith)

/-- Logarithmic height integral throughout the near spectral region. -/
theorem integral_windowError_le_log {η Y r : ℝ} (hη : 0 < η) (hY : 1 ≤ Y)
    (hr : |r| ≤ 4 * Y) :
    (∫ y in Ioc Y (2 * Y), windowError η y r) ≤
      32 * η * Real.log (1 + 6 * Y / η) := by
  have hi (r : ℝ) : IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ => (η + |y - r|)⁻¹) (Ioc Y (2 * Y)) := by
    exact ((continuous_const.add (continuous_id.sub continuous_const).abs).inv₀
      (fun _ => by dsimp; positivity)).integrableOn_Icc.mono_set Ioc_subset_Icc_self
  have hp := integral_endpoint_envelope_le hη hY hr
  have hn := integral_endpoint_envelope_le hη hY (r := -r) (by simpa using hr)
  simp only [sub_neg_eq_add] at hn
  have hs : IntegrableOn (fun y : ℝ =>
      8 * η * (η + |y - r|)⁻¹ + 8 * η * (η + |y - -r|)⁻¹) (Ioc Y (2 * Y)) :=
    ((hi r).const_mul (8 * η)).add ((hi (-r)).const_mul (8 * η))
  have hb := setIntegral_mono_on (integrableOn_windowError hη hY r) hs measurableSet_Ioc
    (fun y hy => by
      change windowError η y r ≤ 8 * η * (η + |y - r|)⁻¹ + 8 * η * (η + |y - -r|)⁻¹
      simpa only [div_eq_mul_inv, sub_neg_eq_add] using
        windowError_le_endpoint_envelope hη (by linarith [hy.1]) (r := r))
  rw [integral_add ((hi r).const_mul _) ((hi (-r)).const_mul _),
    integral_const_mul, integral_const_mul] at hb
  simp only [sub_neg_eq_add] at hb
  nlinarith [mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hp (show 0 ≤ 8 * η by positivity),
    mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hn (show 0 ≤ 8 * η by positivity)]

/-!
# The canonical even logarithmic derivative at one

Proper prime powers are harmonically summable. The even restriction adds
only the single prime two, giving a uniform bound on the closed half-line.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology Set
noncomputable section
namespace RHTower.WeilWorkSettledPhase

private theorem summable_even_vonMangoldt_div :
    Summable (fun n : ℕ => if 2 ∣ n then (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℝ)/n else 0) := by
  have hd : Summable (fun n : ℕ => if n=2 then Real.log 2/2 else 0) :=
    summable_of_ne_finset_zero (s := {2}) fun n hn => by
      simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hn
      simp [hn]
  have hlog : 0 ≤ Real.log (2 : ℝ)/2 :=
    div_nonneg (Real.log_nonneg (by norm_num)) (by norm_num)
  have hs := WeilPrimeDeficit.summable_nonprime_vonMangoldt_div.add hd
  refine hs.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => by split_ifs <;> positivity) fun n => ?_
  by_cases hp : n.Prime
  · by_cases he : 2 ∣ n
    · have hn : n=2 := by
        rcases (Nat.dvd_prime hp).mp he with h | h
        · norm_num at h
        · exact h.symm
      subst n
      simp [Nat.prime_two,ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_prime Nat.prime_two]
    · simp only [hp,he,if_true,if_false,zero_add]
      split_ifs <;> linarith
  · by_cases he : 2 ∣ n
    · simp only [hp,he,if_false,if_true]
      apply le_add_of_nonneg_right
      split_ifs <;> linarith
    · simp only [hp,he,if_false]
      split_ifs <;> positivity

/-- The even restriction of the canonical logarithmic derivative is absolutely
convergent at one. -/
theorem LSeriesSummable_even_vonMangoldt_one :
    LSeriesSummable (evenPart (fun n => (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ))) 1 := by
  apply Summable.of_norm
  refine summable_even_vonMangoldt_div.congr fun n => ?_
  rw [LSeries.norm_term_eq]
  by_cases hn : n=0
  · subst n
    simp
  · by_cases he : 2 ∣ n <;>
      simp [hn,he,evenPart,Complex.norm_real,abs_of_nonneg ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_nonneg]

/-- A uniform bound down to the pole for the even canonical logarithmic derivative. -/
theorem exists_norm_even_vonMangoldt_le :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0≤C ∧ ∀ σ : ℝ, 1≤σ →
      ‖LSeries (evenPart (fun n => (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ))) (σ : ℂ)‖≤C := by
  let f := evenPart (fun n => (ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n : ℂ))
  have hs : LSeriesSummable f 1 := LSeriesSummable_even_vonMangoldt_one
  refine ⟨∑' n, ‖LSeries.term f 1 n‖,tsum_nonneg fun _ => norm_nonneg _,fun σ hσ => ?_⟩
  have hs' : LSeriesSummable f (σ : ℂ) := hs.of_re_le_re (by simpa using hσ)
  exact (norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm hs'.norm).trans
    (hs'.norm.tsum_le_tsum (fun n => LSeries.norm_term_le_of_re_le_re f (by simpa using hσ) n) hs.norm)
